emerging_technology: Text-to-image diffusion models, with latent diffusion as the reference architecture
intended_application: Generate internal advertising concept images and mood boards for homeware campaigns; final product photographs and advertising copy remain separately authored and checked.
organization: A hypothetical U.S. small online homeware retailer with two marketing staff and an owner who approves concepts.
industry_sector: Consumer homeware retail and digital marketing
business_need: Explore visual directions before commissioning a photo shoot; the organization has not yet measured any time or cost savings.
users_stakeholders: Marketing staff, the owner, a freelance designer, and customers who may eventually see separately approved campaign assets.
capabilities_constraints: Staff can edit images and compare ideas with a product catalogue. No in-house ML staff or training compute. An already trained model may be evaluated, but no vendor, model version, price, or license has been selected.
risk_consequence_context: Internal concepts can be discarded. Misleading product appearance, unsupported brand references, or unreviewed publication could create reputational harm. No automatic publication.
management_question: Should this organization adopt, plan a bounded experiment, run a proof of concept, monitor, defer or reject text-to-image diffusion for internal concept boards now? Specify what can start without tool execution and what would change the posture.
time_horizon: Six-week management evidence-gathering horizon. No implied deployment date or forecast market-stage transition.
additional_context:
All organizations are hypothetical exercise assumptions. The U.S. geography and peer definition are explicit scoping choices for Assignment 5, not discovered business facts. No business pilot, employee interview or image-generation experiment has been conducted. Comparable peers would be small U.S. online homeware retailers using internal campaign concept boards. For a future matched peer comparison, the proposed research definition is repeated use in that workflow during the past three months; this definition is not the measure used by the supplied surveys. There is no matched peer denominator or adoption timeline in this packet. No model/vendor has been selected or current input/use conditions cleared. The existing process uses catalogue references, manual boards and a freelance designer before separate final photography. Revenue comes from homeware, not concept images.

Observation: Theoretical framework; not a current adoption survey. https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Diffusion-of-Innovations-5th-Edition/Everett-M-Rogers/9780743222099 Locator: Publisher-hosted excerpt: attributes of innovations; innovativeness and adopter categories; communication and social system. Population/measure: Adoption relative to other members of a specified social system, over time. Supports: Five perceived attributes: relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability and observability. Categories describe relative adoption timing: innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority and laggards. Social influence matters. Limits: Theory does not supply a present-day diffusion stage for image models. Fast follower is a managerial posture, not a sixth Rogers category.
